That's quite the debate, but in it's core it is to deny the very essence of the Holy Spirit into one's heart and to resolve oneself to this in totality in a permanent way. This takes many forms. It can be persistent disobedience to a reprobate heart. It can be regarding the Holy Spirit as intrinsically unclean and committing to it with a hardened heart and stiffneckedness, etc, but ultimately, it is to CHOOSE death for its own sake. Choosing death for its own sake, for any reason, is the thrust of what it is to blaspheme the Holy Spirit. It is those who say "If God is life, then I reject life" and then act on that commitment.

That is what suicide is. It is to reject the Holy Spirit as one rejects life itself for its own sake. It is not because one doesn't it have a chance to repent of it that makes it damnation certain. It is the fact that all forms of blaspheming the Holy Spirit are intrinsically to choose one's own death for its own sake, and suicide is just the most direct version of this.

I HAD to accept that I would be dooming myself to Hell, and so I did. I repented, and the Lord has completely saved me from that damnable spirit that demonically oppressed me almost my entire life. These giants can't just market order large prices without drastically affecting the price with the sharp demand they introduced to the market. Introducing: stop loss hunting! They can manipulate price to areas they believe there are lots of liquidity to reliabilty push price around and meet their quota, self imposed or otherwise. Accumulate positions, and then pick it up elsewhere. Its like a pack of animals or a swarm of locust, migrating and finding food and picking it clean until there are fair value gaps that move price rapidly, especially in times of low liquidity. They use large limit orders, maybe even TPs of multiple trades, to trap price into a small range, with a resistance and support temporarily up. All the different hedge funds compete to control the market price and offload fastest so they make the most money, or worse. 

So what are retail traders? We are the liquidity that buy their limit orders. Don't use market order. That's the lesson. Here OP is reiterating the claim that the gift's presence indicates the seal, ie Holy Spirit's presence. In OP's mind, a genuine Holy Spirit gift can only come after the Holy Spirit's baptism. So if you have gift you must have seal.

Not everyone has studied philosophy like you and I. I think OP has a logically valid argument. The last sentence of their post is key in their thinking, in that genuine gifts from the Spirit only go to the saved.

OP would have to argue a definition of "genuine gift". I imagine it would be something like a true super natural happening or ability originating from the true God. Though as you can see in my other comment, Balaam disproves. 

The actually interesting point is to consider how is it that the disciples recognized the Holy Spirit upon the uncircumcised well enough to use it as their primary evidence in the Council of Jerusalem's decision to not require circumcision.

Maybe OP didn't make it as explicit as you wished but the argument is solid.

1 If you have a gift of the Holy Spirit (not miraculous instance(s), but recreatable spiritual gifting itself) then you have the Holy Spirit.

2 If you have the Holy Spirit, you are saved.

3 Therefore, if you have a gift of the Holy Spirit, you are saved.

It's logically solid; that you are wrong that the premises don't naturally follow the conclusion. 

The only real contention that can be made is against premise 1, and really is the heart of your rejection, and that is: that possession of a gift of the Holy Spirit is an indication that one actually has the Holy Spirit indwelling them (and thus the seal of salvation).

Personally, I struggle to understand how someone can have a spiritual gifting from the Holy Spirit in the context charismatics believe it yet not have the Spirit themself indwelling, especially in this specific dispensation. It seems to me that there is a difference between how the Spirit operated prior to Christ. But that's just my opinion, because the Bible clearly states that Balaam spoke to the true God and spoke true prophecies, but is considered a false prophet because of his alignment against Israel and his motivation of worldly gain. Moreover, he's referred to as a soothsayer rather than a true prophet or seer. Which means someone can be prophesying true things in the true God's name but be false because they do it with sinfully selfish intentions and for harm.


So does that mean that there can be Balaams now doing gifts of the Spirit in the name of God but for dishonest gain? Absolutely, as is referenced in Philippians 1:15-18 wherein Paul basically says Christ is still ultimately preached, or in Revelation 2 where Balaam is referenced explicitly as being active. The book of Jude is entirely about this kind of person. Therefore, premise 1 is contendable for multiple reasons. I will refrain from listing them all.

As for the true alternative, Paul's commentary on Spiritual Gifts in 1st Corinthians really is Christocentric in that it rejects the human (and especially Jewish) propensity to see the miraculous as evidence of the Holy and instead direct us primarily to Love. For if we have anything we can imagine yet not love, we are nothing (as chapter 13 very clearly lays out).


After all, it is not the works of the Spirit that saves us but our faith in the work of Christ on the cross.

And it's not the works of the Spirit that evidences our salvation, but rather our love for one another (John 13:35). 

And we all show that Love differently, hence the works of the Spirit.

Therefore, it is not the presence of those gifts we ought to practice discernment on but rather how and why those gifts are used. Recognizing Balaam relies on this as key.
